record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.context_brief: Defect e ﬀect and independent systems of equations
record.original_question: Is the infinite system of word equations {u_i^1 = v_i^1 v_i^2 ... v_i^n : i >= 0} equivalent to one of its subsystems induced by three equations?

evidence.quote: Is the system {u_i^1 = v_i^1 v_i^2 ··· v_i^n : i >= 0} equivalent to one of its subsystems induced by three equations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. A word equation is a pair $(L,R)$ with $L,R$ words in variables (and possibly constants); a morphism $h:\text{Vars}\to\Sigma^*$ is a solution if $h(L)=h(R)$. Two systems of word equations are called equivalent if they have exactly the same set of solutions. Fix an integer $n\ge 1$ and, for each $i\ge 0$, fix words $u_i^1$ and $v_i^1,v_i^2,\dots,v_i^n$ in some common set of unknowns, giving the infinite system
$$S=\{\,u_i^1 = v_i^1 v_i^2 \cdots v_i^n \;:\; i\ge 0\,\}.$$
Determine whether $S$ is necessarily equivalent to a subsystem consisting of (at most) three of its equations; that is, decide whether for every such $S$ there exist indices $i_1,i_2,i_3\ge 0$ such that the three equations $u_{i_k}^1=v_{i_k}^1\cdots v_{i_k}^n$, $k=1,2,3$, have the same set of solutions as the whole system $S$.
artifact.category_tag: Word equations and combinatorics on words
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on independent systems of word equations indicate that, although every infinite system is equivalent to a finite subsystem (Ehrenfeucht compactness via Hilbert's basis theorem), the precise bound — conjectured to be three for many natural classes of equations of this shape — remains open in general; only partial results (e.g., bounds like 18 for three-variable systems) are known.

status_evidence.title: Independent Systems of Word Equations: From Ehrenfeucht to Eighteen
status_evidence.snippet: Every infinite system of word equations is equivalent to a finite subsystem; the maximal size of an independent system in three unknowns is conjectured small but only bounded by 18, and remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The maximal size of an independent system of constant-free word equations is open beyond trivial cases, supporting that the three-equation reduction question is unresolved.
